title: Health
summary: Medical records for each family member: visits, medicines, allergies, vaccinations and documents. Private by default.

sections.title: People and who can open them

blocks.text: Health keeps one record for each person. A person can be a member with an account, or someone without one, such as a young child. At the top of Health, choose a person to open their record.

To see a person you need two things: Health access in your permissions, and access to that person. The administrator gives both. Access to a person is either **Can view** (read the record and the emergency card) or **Can change** (also edit, upload, export and decide about AI). A person you have no access to does not appear at all.

blocks.title: Adding a person
items: Press **Add person**.
Type the name. You can add a birth date, sex, blood type and notes.
Add up to 3 emergency contacts with their relationship and phone number.
Press **Save person**.

blocks.text: Health is protected with an extra check. See [Account and security](account-security#confirm).
A visit is one trip to a doctor. Open a person and press **Add visit**. Fill in the **Date** and the **Specialty**. You can add the doctor, a diagnosis and notes, and attach documents.
You can see the record **By specialty** (a folder for each kind of doctor) or as a **Timeline**. In the timeline you can filter vaccinations or documents.
The page locks after a period of inactivity. If it locks before you save, long notes that were not saved can be lost. Save often.

Press **Add medication** and type the name. You can add the dose (for example 5 mg), the schedule (for example one tablet in the morning), and the start and end dates. Leave the end date empty if the medicine continues.
Ended medications are hidden. Press **Show ended medications** to see them.

Press **Add allergy**. Type the substance and choose a severity: **Mild**, **Moderate**, **Severe** or **Not specified**. You can add the reaction. If a person has no allergies, simply leave the list empty.
Press **Add vaccination**, type the vaccine and the date it was given. Add **Next due** if another dose is needed.

Members who can change this record get a reminder before the next date. The reminder names the person only, not the vaccine. A due or overdue vaccination is marked on the record. When it is done, press **Mark as given**.
You can keep lab results, reports and photos of paper documents with a person's record.

blocks.title: Where to click
items: Open the person, then press **Add document**. Or open a visit and press **Attach document**.
Choose one or more files. You can add up to 10 at a time.
Give each one a name and, if you like, attach it to a visit.
Press **Add document**.
Allowed formats: PDF, JPG, PNG, WebP and HEIC (the iPhone photo format).
Each file can be up to 10 MB. One person can have up to 200 documents.
Photos are saved as a resized copy, and the place and camera details in them are removed. PDF and HEIC files are saved as they are.
Some photo formats have no preview. Then use **Download document** to see the original.

blocks.text: Open a document in a new tab or download it from its page. Documents are never reachable by an address that anyone can open: only members with access to the person can view them. For more than 10 files, see [Uploading many documents at once](health#bulk-upload).
When you have a pile of paper, scan or photograph it all and add it as one batch. The AI reads the documents one after another and you check what it found, one document at a time.

blocks.title: Where to click
items: Open the person, then press **Upload many documents**. Only members who may change that person's health records see this button.
If the AI notice appears, read it and confirm. The person's AI consent must be on, as for **Run AI**.
Choose your files. Reading starts on the first document while the rest are still uploading.
Watch the list: each document is waiting, being read by the AI, paused, ready, failed or done. You can start reviewing the first ready document straight away.

blocks.title: Reviewing each document
items: Compare the findings with the document. Press **Approve** or **Reject** on each finding. You can edit an approved finding before you continue.

Press **Continue**. Approved findings are saved as records and rejected ones are discarded. Findings you have not decided stay on the document, so you can review them later, and the next document opens.

If the scan is poor, open **Improve the scan**, change brightness, contrast or black and white, and press **Scan again**. That reads the document again and clears the approve and reject marks you had set on it, without asking first.
A person has one unfinished batch at a time. A batch holds up to 50 files, each up to 10 MB, in PDF, JPG, PNG, WebP or HEIC.
Unfinished documents count toward the person's 200 documents, but they do not appear in the person's documents or in search until they are finished.
The AI reads one document at a time. If the AI allowance is used up, the status says paused until a time, and reading continues by itself.
Scan again is allowed 5 times per document. Every scan is a new AI run and shows in Settings, AI calls (administrators only).
Brightness, contrast and black and white change only the copy sent to the AI. Your stored original is never changed. The settings are remembered for that document.
A document the AI could not read can be tried again, kept without findings (only offered for failed documents), or removed from the batch.

blocks.text: You can close the browser and carry on later, on this or another device: the batch is still on the person's page. An unfinished batch and its unfinished documents are deleted 30 days after the batch was started, unless a document already has accepted findings, which is kept; finished documents and saved records always stay. The person's AI consent and the AI notice apply as for **Run AI**. If you turn AI off for the person, waiting and queued reading is cancelled and recognised text is removed, but the documents and the choices you made stay. When you turn AI on again, the batch continues. Only members who may change the person's health records can see and use a batch, and its actions are written to the audit log.

On the Health page, above the folders and the timeline, there is a box **Search documents**. It finds documents by their name and by the words inside them. The box appears when there is something to search, and it is not on the page when no person is shown.

blocks.title: Where to click
items: Type at least two letters in the box. One letter is not enough, and nothing is searched until there are two.
Wait a moment, or press Enter or **Search**, to see the results.
Choose **Search in** to look in **All people** or only in the person you have open. This choice appears only when you can see more than one person.
Press a result to open that document. Press **Clear search** (or Escape in the box) to go back to the folders and the timeline.
A result shows the document name, the person, the date it was added, the visit it belongs to and the page where the words were found, with the matching words highlighted.
Accents and word endings do not matter much: typing a word without accents, or in a slightly different form, still finds it.
AI reads a document only when someone asked it to. A document AI never read is found by its name only. Documents AI did read are also found by the words inside them.

You only ever see documents you may open. A document of a person you cannot see, or an archived document, is never found, and you get the same "No documents found" as for a word that is simply not there.
If a result says **Only the first pages are searched**, AI read only the beginning of a long document, so words further on are not found.

If a note says that some words of your search were not used, those words were skipped: words of one letter, words without Latin letters or digits (such as Chinese) and every word after the eighth. The other words were searched.

blocks.text: The text was read by AI and may contain mistakes. A word can be missed if it was misread. When the page says so, it shows a note above the results. If a search finds nothing, look at the document itself.
The words you type are used only for this search. They are not saved, not kept in the address of the page and not remembered after you leave the page.
When AI has read a document, the text it read is saved and shown in the panel of the document under **Recognised text**. It is what makes the document searchable by its words.

blocks.title: Where to click
items: Open the document. The **Recognised text** section is closed at first.
Press **Recognised text** to open it. The text is loaded only now and is read page by page.
Press **Copy text** to copy all of it. For a document with more pages, each page after the first starts with a blank line and its page label.
Press **Recognised text** again to close it. The text is not kept in the browser.
Everyone who may open the document can read and copy its recognised text. A member who can only view the person sees it too, but cannot remove it.
It can contain mistakes: a note says "May contain errors" while that is the case, and the text says it was read by AI. Check the document itself when it matters.
If AI read only the first pages of a long document, a note says "First 3 of 8 pages", for example. Only those pages are searchable.

A member who can change the person can press **Remove recognised text** and confirm. The text is deleted from the app. The document and the suggestions you already accepted stay, and the document is no longer found by the words inside it. You can run AI again to read it later.
Copies in backups are removed when the backups expire.
The text is deleted with the document. It is hidden together with archived documents and archived people.

If AI is turned off for a person who has recognised text, you are asked first, and then the recognised text of that person's documents is deleted too. The documents can then be found by their names only.

blocks.text: While AI is reading a document again, you can still read the earlier text, and a line tells you that a new reading is in progress. As soon as the new reading has saved its first pages, the section shows that text instead; a long document is saved a few pages at a time, and a note says when only the first pages were read. See also [AI help and your consent](health#ai).

sections.title: Printing and exports for a doctor

blocks.title: Where to click
items: Open the person and choose **Export records**.
Under **What to include**, choose **Everything for this person** or **One specialty**.
Under **Format**, choose **For a doctor**, **Data file** or **For AI**.
Press **Create export**. For a doctor, a printable page opens: press **Print export** and choose **Save as PDF** to get a file.
**For a doctor**: a clean printable page.
**Data file**: a structured file (JSON) to keep or move elsewhere.
**For AI**: a Markdown file with the name and birth date left out. Notes and diagnoses are copied as written and may still mention the person, so check it before you share it.

blocks.text: Exports are made when you ask and are not stored on the server. Anything an AI suggested and nobody has checked is only included if you tick that option, and is marked **Unverified**.

The emergency card is a one-page summary: allergies, current medications and emergency contacts. Open it with **Open emergency card** on the person's page and press **Print card** to print it. Check that it is up to date before you rely on it.
A health record can be deleted for good only shortly after it was created. By default that is 72 hours. The family administrator sets this time in the server settings.

After that time, **Delete** becomes **Archive**. An archived item is kept but hidden everywhere: in lists, exports, the emergency card, reminders and AI. Members who can change the person can find it again under **Archived items** and press **Restore**.
Not sure if an entry is right? Archive it instead of deleting it. You can bring it back.
AI can read a document and suggest visits, medications, allergies and vaccinations, so you type less. It is optional.

AI is off until the administrator has set it up and turned it on, and it is off for every person until a member switches it on. When AI is used, the document leaves this server and is sent to an outside company (OpenAI, or GitHub if OpenAI is not available). That company may keep it under its own terms.

Where full-text reading is turned on (the notice you see says so), AI reads a document in two steps. First the pictures of up to 20 pages are sent and AI reads all the text. Then the text that was read is sent as well and AI makes suggestions from it. Both go to the company named in the notice. The text is saved in this app's database and shown under **Recognised text** in the document panel. Every member who may open the document can search it. It is kept until the document is deleted or the text is removed, and it stays in backups until they expire.

items: Each person has a switch **Allow AI to read documents of this person**. It is off by default. A member who can change that person decides, and sees a clear question before turning it on. Turn it off at any time.
AI never runs by itself on a document. Someone presses **Run AI** and sees a notice that names the company the document will be sent to.

AI reads PDF files up to their first 20 pages and photos, including HEIC photos from an iPhone. A HEIC photo is turned into an ordinary picture on the server only for the AI run; the stored original is not changed and the place and camera details are not sent.
When the suggestions are ready, press **Review suggestions**. Nothing is saved until you press **Accept** on an entry. You can **Edit** or **Reject** it.
Everything AI suggested is marked **Unverified** until a person presses **Mark as verified**. AI can be wrong, so always compare it with the document.

The first time you run AI after this was turned on, a new notice is shown once more, and you confirm it before the document is sent. It says that the text is saved here. An administrator confirms the same notice before starting a bulk run.

If the document already has complete recognised text, **Run AI** makes suggestions from it and does not send the pages again. To have the document read again, remove the text first (see [Recognised text of a document](health#recognised-text)).

A run that only reads the text, such as a bulk run for documents without recognised text, shows the tag **Text saved**. It makes no suggestions and shows no **Review suggestions** button. Press **Run AI** to get suggestions.

If AI is switched off for a person, no new run starts and runs that were waiting are stopped. When that person has recognised text, you are told first that it will be deleted, and the documents are then found by their names only.

blocks.text: If AI is not available, you will see a short message, and you can always add the details yourself. The administrator can see a list of AI calls, but never what was in a document.
